entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Final War of the Roman Republic was a pivotal conflict that marked the end of the Roman Republic and the transition to the Roman Empire.

This war, fought between the Optimates and the Populares, was the culmination of a series of civil wars that had plagued the Roman Republic since the late 2nd century BCE.

The war was sparked by the rivalry between the two main factions, led by the consuls Lucius Cornelius Cinna and Gaius Marius, who were vying for power and control over the Roman state.

The war raged on for several years, with both sides suffering heavy losses, until the death of Marius in 101 BCE.

The Optimates, led by Sulla, ultimately emerged victorious, but their victory came at a great cost, as the Roman Republic was irreparably damaged, paving the way for the rise of the Roman Empire.

The legacy of the Final War of the Roman Republic can be seen in the establishment of the Roman Empire and the end of the Roman Republic.

"The Roman Empire was a great and terrible thing." - Tacitus, The Histories
